crop.notes: Whole article with headline, three pieces.

title.suggested: Tom Allen Knocked Out by Dan Daly in Street Fight

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic reported that Dan Daly knocked Tom Allen down in a street fight outside Daly's Seventh Street saloon after Allen accused him of hurting his business. Allen and Charley Daly were arrested and bonded.

metadata.notes: Masthead: 'The Republic: St. Louis, Mo., Monday Morning, June 18, 1888', page 8.

facts.fact: About 1:30 a.m., Dan Daly, champion middleweight of Missouri, knocked Allen down in a street fight in front of Daly's saloon on Seventh Street between Market and Chestnut; Allen cried 'enough'
places: Seventh Street between Market and Chestnut, St. Louis

facts.fact: The fight began when Allen, chasing men who had called him names, accused Dan Daly of hiding them and of doing things to hurt his business
Allen and Charley Daly were taken to the Chestnut Street police station and released on bond

notes: Account is from spectators friendly to the Dalys ('it is said', 'it is alleged'). The current title reads as if Allen knocked out Daly.
